overview: South Africa is the southernmost country in Africa. It has three capital cities, Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein, while Johannesburg is its largest city. From 1948 to the early 1990s it was ruled under apartheid, a system of racial segregation; in 1994 it held its first democratic elections and Nelson Mandela became president. It has 12 official languages.

geography.text: South Africa has coasts on both the Atlantic and Indian oceans, which meet near its southern tip. Much of the interior is a high plateau called the Highveld, edged by the Great Escarpment, including the Drakensberg mountains. The west is dry, while the east is greener. Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town, and Kruger National Park is one of Africa's largest wildlife reserves.

history.text: The ancestors of the San and Khoekhoe lived in South Africa for many thousands of years, and Bantu-speaking peoples arrived later. The Dutch founded Cape Town in 1652, and Britain took over the Cape in 1806. Diamonds and gold brought wealth and war. From 1948 the apartheid system enforced racial segregation, until Nelson Mandela was elected president in 1994.

events.title: Cape Town
events.text: The Dutch East India Company founds a supply station.

events.title: Battle of Isandlwana
events.text: The Zulu army defeats British forces.

events.title: Gold rush
events.text: Gold is found on the Witwatersrand; Johannesburg grows.

events.title: Democracy
events.text: Nelson Mandela becomes president after the first free elections.

government.text: South Africa is a parliamentary republic. Parliament elects the President, who is head of state and government. The African National Congress governed alone from 1994 until 2024, when it lost its majority and formed a coalition. South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

economy.text: South Africa has one of the most developed economies in Africa. It is the world's largest producer of platinum and a major producer of gold, coal and chromium. It has a large financial sector based in Johannesburg, but unemployment is very high.

culture.text: South Africa has 12 official languages, including Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans and English, and is called the 'Rainbow Nation'. Nelson Mandela, imprisoned for 27 years, became its first Black president. Archbishop Desmond Tutu and Mandela both won the Nobel Peace Prize.

items.title: Robben Island
items.text: Where Mandela was imprisoned, now a museum.

items.title: Table Mountain
items.text: A flat-topped mountain above Cape Town.

items.title: Cradle of Humankind
items.text: Caves with some of the oldest human fossils.

sport.text: Rugby, football and cricket are the biggest sports. The Springboks have won the Rugby World Cup a record four times. South Africa hosted the 2010 football World Cup, the first in Africa. Wayde van Niekerk holds the 400 m world record.

items.text: Hosted the first men's World Cup in Africa.
